data.title: 'Space being weaponised': A purely civilian system can be 'repurposed' for military capabilities
data.description: Erin Ogunkeye is pleased to welcome Mélusine Lebret, Researcher in the Defence, Security & Justice research group at RAND Europe. According to Lebret, the growing militarisation of space cannot be understood simply by asking whether a satellite is civilian, military, or a “weaponised.” And Lebreton argues that militarization does not eliminate the necessity of cooperation. The emerging space-security order is therefore defined by an unusual tension: states may increasingly prepare to compete and potentially fight in space while remaining structurally dependent on one another to keep space usable at all.

data.title: ‘I thank God for killing me and bringing me back’: Nicolas Winding Refn on the emergency op that inspired his new sci-fi horror
data.description: Notorious for ultra-violent movies like Drive and The Neon Demon, the Dane had lost the will to direct until ‘the Tom Cruise of surgeons’ saved his life – and triggered an astonishing creative rebirth Nicolas Winding Refn has his phone out, showing me one of the goriest scenes he’s ever been involved in. Given that the Danish director’s movies have involved hands getting sliced off, eyeballs being gouged out and a son reaching deep inside his mother’s womb, that’s certainly saying something. In this video, the camera is fixed upon a beating heart when suddenly – slash! – it gets sliced open with a knife. We travel into the open chamber, as needles arrive to pierce through the muscle. Unsettling and compelling, could this be a future Palme d’Or winner? Unlikely. You see, Refn isn’t the director of this footage; he’s actually the guy lying conked out in the operating room while a surgeon attends to him. Requesting that someone films your own heart surgery is a very Nicolas Winding Refn thing to do. “At first they said no,” says the film-maker known for Drive, Bronson and The Neon Demon. “But then they said, ‘As it’s you, we’ll record it.’” Continue reading...

data.title: Can fish and chip shops survive? ‘We made more money by closing than staying open’
data.description: Soaring fish prices, labour costs and changing tastes all spell bad news for Britain’s chippies. Is this the end for the seaside staple – or will a few innovators succeed in keeping them alive? One day in 2007, Darren Sudlow drove past the old stationmaster’s house at Padgate station, in Cheshire, noticed it was empty and decided to lease it. “He just fell in love with the place,” says his son, Kieran, who was 11 at the time. “He said he always wanted a fish and chip shop, for some reason.” Despite having worked as a joiner up to that point, Darren made a go of it, and the Plaice Station, as he named it, was a success from day one. “He worked like mad to get it open and then realised that the hard work hadn’t even started, and he had a queue out the door,” says the younger Sudlow. The family lived nearby. Kieran Sudlow, who is now 30, worked at the Plaice Station as a boy, peeling potatoes, washing dishes after school, then cooking at the range when he was 16. He went on to become a chef, working in Australia for a few years, then returning to help out at the chippy part-time when needed. Business had always been pretty good. They won local awards and had a loyal customer base. But one day in March, Kieran remembers, his father came in and told him: “‘I think the fish and chip shop’s going to go.’ He said, ‘It’s not making money. I can’t see it carrying on.’” Continue reading...

data.title: ‘When you tell people the story, it’s almost too good to be true’: the incredible journey behind The Cycle of Love
data.description: Documentary director Orlando von Einsiedel on how the real life tale of a man who cycles 6,000 miles from India to Sweden to find his true love will warm your heart New Delhi, December 1975. It was love at first sight when a Swedish hippy called Lotta von Schedvin sat down to be sketched by an Indian street artist, Pradyumna Kumar Mahanandia, known to everyone as PK. In the 10 minutes it took PK to complete her portrait, everything clicked into place for the pair. They were swept headlong in a whirlwind romance, and PK took Lotta to his village in the east of India to meet his family. But soon after, the time came for Lotta to pack up her VW campervan and head back home with her friends. Heart-stricken PK promised to follow, but a plane ticket to Sweden was an impossible dream. Determined not to lose the love of his life, PK bought a secondhand Raleigh bike, and with $80 sewn into the waistband of his trousers, set off to cycle 6,000 miles to Lotta . He knew the sun set in the west, so that was the direction he took. His plan was to follow the hippy trail, cycling through India, Pakistan, Afghanistan, Iran and Turkey, crossing Europe, finally arriving in Sweden. Continue reading...

data.title: ‘Like a Disney movie’: Three wild dog brothers make Africa’s longest journey
data.description: As three siblings came of age and had to leave their pack, scientists tracked the dogs’ perilous 2,500-mile odyssey to find their own territory It sounds like a Disney movie: three wild dogs, all brothers, on an epic journey to find a home of their own after their family tells them to leave. They dodge cars and hunters in search of a new life, navigating bushmeat snares and the hostility of a human-dominated landscape until they find a new haven on the African savannah. But this is exactly what happened in Zambia last year, when three endangered African wild dogs made the longest-ever recorded single journey of any mammal from the continent. The brothers travelled more than 2,500 miles (4,100km) over eight months in their “dispersal” – when a young dog comes of age and must establish new territory to find a mate and start a family of their own. data.title: Faster! Louder! Brighter! How the attention economy overwhelmed children’s TV
data.description: Does your child’s favourite show give them a chance to reflect, or does it move too quickly for its lessons to sink in? A version of this piece was originally published on Aeon as The bombarding of childhood I am at the airport gate waiting to depart, watching passengers hurry past with rolling suitcases and paper cups of coffee. A small boy sits very still beside his mother. He holds an iPad close to his chest, almost in a cramp, clutching the screen as if it might otherwise run away. I hear loud clapping hands and squeaking children’s voices. I lean over and see a cartoon character in green snatch a toy from another character in pink. The pink character begins to cry, tears splashing like sprinkles from its enormous eyes. The green character shouts sorry. Instantly, the tears stop and a wide smile replaces them before I have blinked. And, before I have even worked out whether the characters are speaking English or Arabic (as the mother does to the boy), the scene has changed and the two characters are rowing a boat with a random song in the background. The boy’s eyes dart on the screen from right to left, centre, down. His body is still but his attention is being hurried from cue to cue. This is the problem I have come to think of as the pace of children’s media. Continue reading...

data.title: ‘Made in Europe’ law threatens UK plans for reset with EU
data.description: Government sources say legislation aimed at China poses a risk to British businesses and must be addressed The UK government’s EU reset summit will be delayed again unless the bloc agrees to discuss legislation that could lock British business out of parts of EU industry, government sources have said. The “Made in Europe” legislation – formally known as the Industrial Accelerator Act – is designed to curb China’s increasing presence in European industry, but was not on the reset plan agreed by the former prime minister Keir Starmer and the European Commission chief, Ursula von der Leyen, in London in May 2025. data.title: Bad Apples review – Saoirse Ronan’s suffering teacher best thing about school horror-satire
data.description: Ronan plays a teacher who finds a way to deal with a disruptive pupil in Jonatan Etzler’s implausible film, but it’s not shocking or funny enough Here is a strange, heavy-handed and unpersuasive black comedy which owes what success it has to the star-power of its lead, Saoirse Ronan, who is incapable of giving an uninteresting performance. Director Jonatan Etzler has adapted it with co-screenwriter Jess O’Kane from a Swedish novel by Rasmus Lindgren called De Oönskade, or The Unwanted, and is a film that asks you to overlook its plot-holes and implausibilities on the grounds that it is a satire – but a satire saying what, exactly? The scene is a primary school in the English West Country where Maria (Ronan) is a hardworking, idealistic teacher – but her class is hopelessly disrupted by a violent boy, Danny (Eddie Walker), obnoxious and out of control. He seriously injures another pupil, the nerdy teacher’s-pet Pauline (Nia Brown) whom Maria privately considers a bit annoying. After a chaotic visit to Danny’s home, Marie winds up causing the boy to lose consciousness with an accidental chokehold, and in a panic smuggles him back to her house where she imprisons him in her basement. And then, slowly but surely, the rest of the class, freed from Danny’s hateful presence, blossom and Maria gets a glowing Ofsted report. She looks and feels on top of the world. But what is to be done about her shameful secret? Continue reading...

data.title: ‘You think you’re done and you get pigeonholed’: Samantha Morton on raving, Richard Russell and having another shot as a singer
data.description: The actor and musician spoke at our Guardian Live ‘Honest Playlist’ event at Green Man festival about growing up in Nottingham on the free-party scene, and the healing powers of music On the Sunday afternoon of Green Man Festival in August, Samantha Morton joined me onstage in the Talking Shop tent to discuss her life in music. The celebrated actor and director is currently in cinemas as the scene-stealing Cerce in The Odyssey , but she is also a musician. Later that day, she performed on the main stage later with Everything Is Recorded, the supergroup led by XL label boss Richard Russell, who also collaborated with Morton on her 2024 solo album Daffodils & Dirt . More recently, she voiced her character’s title song on The Odyssey soundtrack. “I love talking about music,” she says. “I never really get asked enough to talk about music.” For this in-depth conversation with Guardian Live, Morton took us through her Honest Playlist of songs on various themes that have meant something to her, including the first single she bought, Musical Youth’s reggae-pop hit Pass The Dutchie, the song she’d do at karaoke, Michael Prophet and Ricky Tuffy’s Your Love, and a great song to fall in love to (Moments In Love by Art of Noise). She thinks about playlists often, revealing that she makes them whenever she needs to get into character for a role and used to “carry tapes in my back pocket everywhere I went because I couldn’t have bad music.” Continue reading...

data.title: Hard parties, cheap rents and horrible flats: how 90s art and fashion redefined British culture
data.description: An evocative new Tate Britain show captures an era when the UK’s newly flush creative industries teamed up with a generation of skint dreamers to bring the decade into vivid colour Here is Kate Moss, with pink hair splayed across a pillow, her face scrubbed of makeup, her smile sweet and wonky. Sarah Lucas’s Pauline Bunny artwork with its confrontational hosiery on a charity shop chair. Sean Ellis’s collaborative knights-in-grubby-armour shoot with Alexander McQueen. Here are happy ravers, in a club, or saluting the sun as it stretches and yawns over a litter-strewn hill. These photos are old. They were taken a long time ago. But they’re young, too. They are curated by Edward Enninful for the Tate’s exhibition The 90s: Art and Fashion (Enninful worked at i-D in the 90s) and almost everyone involved is shiny and fresh. The models, whether professional or not, are mostly in their 20s, and the photographers are early in their careers. It gives the photos a youthful fizz, a verve. But the energy also comes from an understanding between photographer and subject. In many of the pictures you can feel the shared mischief, a “yes we’re serious about our ideas” but also a “look, we’re getting away with it!” delight. Continue reading...

data.title: Driving that’s too fast, too dangerous and utterly lawless: why do we tolerate this petro-masculinity? | George Monbiot
data.description: In towns and in the countryside, I see SUVs and pickup trucks driven without care or conscience. It’s the Magafication of transport Where is lawbreaking not just visible, but designed to be seen? Where is antisocial behaviour worn as a badge of honour? Where is pleasure gained directly from causing distress? And where is reckless endangerment often ignored by the police or treated with the mildest of punishments? The answer is on the roads. Last month, three men in the West Midlands were convicted of street racing. Two were driving at over 80mph in a 40mph zone. The third clocked over 90mph in a 30mph zone. The West Midlands has long been blighted by organised racing , sometimes involving 200 cars or more and hundreds of spectators. The result is a long catalogue of deaths and life-changing injuries, including some caused when racers have left the road and ploughed into onlookers or pedestrians . And there are plenty more accidents where the police have little idea whether racing is to blame, for as soon as they happen, the drivers disperse. George Monbiot is a Guardian columnist Continue reading...

data.title: How’s your apocalypse stockpiling coming on? Three weeks in, mine has hit a few snags | Emma Brockes
data.description: Cans of tuna, sparkling water and an old torch – if the end of the world came for me now I’d struggle, but it’s hard to know how to prepare for an unknown threat It’s been three weeks since the government advisory urging us to start stockpiling in case of emergency – how’s your prep coming along? The Prepare campaign, backed by Wes Streeting, who one imagines gliding through the apocalypse, quiff undisturbed, listed nine essential items, among them wet wipes, first-aid kits and batteries. The World Health Organization, meanwhile, suggests budgeting for 15 litres of water per person per day, so a family of four will need to store upwards of 180 litres to cover the recommended period of three days. The chances of this actually happening seem to me, intuitively, to be considerably lower than the disaster they’re supposed to forestall. But hope springs, so let’s see. The first step towards stockpiling is stocktaking. This is where I’m at: one mega-torch (uncharged), which I bought in prepper mode after surviving the terrifying New York blackout of 2019 when for about an hour we couldn’t charge our phones; lots of very large sticking plasters and a handful of small round ones, the normal sizes having long been used up; two cans of tuna, which will go down to one after lunch; two litres of sparkling water, so for the first hour or so after a nuclear strike, assuming it happens this afternoon, we’ll at least be able to enjoy some bubbles; and three OxyContin saved from my c-section almost 12 years ago, which are probably less powerful than homeopathy at this point but I retain a vague hope I can use for barter when money breaks down. Emma Brockes is a Guardian columnist Continue reading...

data.title: The Guardian view on Sweden’s election result: an opportunity that progressive parties must not squander | Editorial
data.description: After a desperately tight race, voters rejected the prospect of the far right in government. A potential centre-left coalition needs to seize the moment European progressives searching for reasons to be cheerful have been finding them hard to come by this autumn. In Germany, the dramatic rise of the Alternative für Deutschland party is threatening the liberal values that underpin the identity of the federal republic. In France, polls continue to point to a likely Marine Le Pen victory in a presidential election , which is months away. Across mainland Europe, centre-left parties are failing to muster an adequate response to nativist movements that have colonised swathes of the working-class support that they once relied on. In such an ominous political landscape, the outcome of a cliffhanger Swedish election provides a much‑needed source of optimism – albeit one that comes with heavy caveats. Prior to last Sunday’s poll, the outgoing prime minister, Ulf Kristersson, was explicit that if his rightwing alliance won the largest number of seats, he would invite members of the far-right Sweden Democrats party (SD) to become ministers in the next government. Do you have an opinion on the issues raised in this article? In Germany, the dramatic rise of the Alternative für Deutschland party is threatening the liberal values that underpin the identity of the federal republic. In France, polls continue to point to a likely Marine Le Pen victory in a presidential election , which is months away. Across mainland Europe, centre-left parties are failing to muster an adequate response to nativist movements that have colonised swathes of the working-class support that they once relied on. In such an ominous political landscape, the outcome of a cliffhanger Swedish election provides a much‑needed source of optimism – albeit one that comes with heavy caveats. Prior to last Sunday’s poll, the outgoing prime minister, Ulf Kristersson, was explicit that if his rightwing alliance won the largest number of seats, he would invite members of the far-right Sweden Democrats party (SD) to become ministers in the next government. data.title: The Guardian view on the Houthi advance in Yemen: another vital Middle East artery becomes a battlefield | Editorial
data.description: The extraordinary success of the rebels, and Saudi counterstrikes, threaten economic havoc. But the country’s civilians are paying the highest price Even in a region beset by turmoil and learning to expect the unexpected, the lightning advance of Yemen’s Houthis along the Red Sea coast has shocked observers. More than 100,000 people have been forced to flee in a country where immiseration and displacement have become routine and half the population depend on humanitarian aid. But outsiders are paying close attention, because by claiming thousands of kilometres in a matter of days, and seizing strategically important islands, the Iran-backed rebels now control the Bab al-Mandab strait – the other major regional energy chokepoint after the Hormuz strait. The Iran war has forced Saudi Arabia to rely on moving oil via its east-west pipeline to Red Sea ports. Now drone strikes – blamed on an Iran-backed militia in Iraq – have shut the pipeline: on one estimate , a month-long closure could cut global crude supply by 120m barrels. The halt to shipping through the Bab al-Mandab strait could be much more protracted. Taking the oil north is a far slower and more expensive route to Asian markets, and does not preclude attacks by the Houthis, who are also targeting oil facilities. data.title: LeBron James once raged against the machine. Increasingly, he helps prop it up
data.description: LeBron James was once one of the world’s most outspoken athletes. Now he’s plugging a predictions market and an authoritarian leader There was a time when LeBron James’s views on abuses of political power were considered dangerous enough that Donald Trump’s allies told him to shut up and dribble. But over time, James has become less outspoken. After he built a reputation as a voice on social issues and human rights, anti-government protesters in Hong Kong burned his jersey over what they saw as his lack of support for their campaign. Alongside plenty of other US athletes, he has barely spoken on politics during Trump’s second term in power. There was the recent dismal sight of him promoting a prediction market (although at least he kept his clothes on ). Now he is happily associating with – and helping promote – an authoritarian leader. On Sunday, Angola’s president, João Lourenço, welcomed two of the most famous people in America – James and Will Smith – to his presidential palace. Continue reading...

Black holes are objects so densely compact that beyond a certain point their gravity is too strong for light and matter to escape. This boundary of no return is known as the event horizon – the point at which escaping would require something to travel faster than the speed of light. Continue reading...

data.title: Datacenter rush will create ‘tsunami’ of discarded electronics, report says
data.description: Global push will triple toxic e-waste annually in 25 years, filling enough shipping containers to circle globe six times The ongoing campaign to build thousands of massive datacenters for AI will create a “tsunami” of discarded electronics, putting the world on a course to triple its annual generation of toxic e-waste in the next 25 years, a new report projects. The electronic trash AI generates in the next 25 years could fill enough shipping containers to encircle the globe six times, it said. Yet, says the report by the non-profit environmental group Basel Action Network (BAN), there is no plan to deal with that waste – which typically contains toxins like lead, mercury, cadmium and forever chemicals, as well as valuable metals that are challenging to reclaim. Continue reading...

data.title: House votes to hold Leon Black in contempt over Epstein subpoenas refusal
data.description: Billionaire has refused to comply with subpoenas from House oversight committee as part of Epstein inquiry US politics live – latest updates The House of Representatives voted on Wednesday to hold billionaire investor Leon Black in contempt of Congress over his refusal to comply with subpoenas issued to him by the House oversight committee as part of its investigation into Jeffrey Epstein. The action came a day after the committee voted unanimously to recommend that the House hold Black in contempt. Wednesday’s House vote passed under unanimous consent, meaning there was not a formal roll call, but no member objected to the contempt resolution . Continue reading...

data.title: Kosovo’s former president jailed for 25 years over war crimes
data.description: Hashim Thaçi, 58, was convicted by The Hague for crimes committed while he was senior commander of the Kosovo Liberation Army Hashim Thaçi, the former president of Kosovo, has been sentenced to 25 years in prison by a tribunal in The Hague for war crimes, including dozens of murders, committed during his time as a senior commander of the Kosovo Liberation Army during the country’s war for independence from Serbia in the late 1990s. The European-backed Kosovo Specialist Chambers, convicted Thaci, 58, and three other former senior commanders of 96 murders, and counts of torture, cruel treatment and arbitrary detention directed at political opponents and civilians. data.title: England ’Til I Die review – a chilling portrait of a town turning on its neighbours
data.description: Film-maker Jamie Roberts follows a Sussex man’s journey into the far right. If it wasn’t so horrific, parts could feel like they’d been written by Chris Morris Standing in the street shouting virulent slogans or chanting loaded refrains about Islam was the mainstay of British far-right groups such as the EDL in the early 2010s. Now, that behaviour feels almost quaint. Recent weeks have seen major anti-immigration blockades in Dover led by balaclava-wearing men, and direct action against asylum seekers arriving on a small boat in Portsmouth. Clearly, in 2026, the blame for much of the societal rot that has set in has been placed frequently at the feet of migrants, and vigilante tactics are on the rise. Channel 4’s one-off documentary arrives with depressing timeliness, then, telling a story that serves as a synecdoche for events playing out across the UK, at large. It is, says its maker, “the story of a community on the frontline of Britain’s broken asylum system, and one man’s journey into the heart of the far-right movement”. Continue reading...

data.title: The secret of Mozart’s genius unlocked – has a teenager succeeded where generations of musicologists have failed?
data.description: US student Linus Chen-Plotkin has analysed music by four canonical composers looking for patterns. Turns out Mozart’s music moves in the least predictable way It’s a question that has taxed musical thinkers for centuries: just what is it about one composer’s music that makes it more distinctive than anyone else’s? Entire disciplines of academic thought, of music analysis and historical musicology, as well as the formation of classical music’s canon of “great” composers, have been given over to this single idea: can it be proved that Mozart, say, was measurably “better” than other composers? Our instinctive feeling about the sensual magic of Mozart’s music is part of the equation, but accounting for precisely how his pieces can sustain a lifetime of listening, why their pleasures never seem to pall and are still capable of seeming to surprise us even when we know them inside out: that’s the million-dollar musicological question. Continue reading...

data.title: South Park – I mean, South America – is back, with no Donald Trump in sight (yet)
data.description: After adopting the president’s fondness for renaming things ‘America’, the season 29 premiere sees Trey Parker and Matt Stone use e-bikes to critique the ruination of the US South Park has been renamed South America. That was the main news ahead of Trey Parker and Matt Stone’s animated series returning for its 29th season, which seemed like it could be a one-off promotional gag – or another Trump-related storyline after last year’s scorching imitation of the US president’s “renaming” of the Gulf of Mexico and Lake Ontario . It turns out that neither is exactly the case, at least not so far. The season premiere doesn’t see the South Park sign scribbled over by the president’s dumb-guy sharpie pen. But it’s not just a passing sight gag, either. The six-episode season opens with the renaming already a fait accompli, not even commented on. Continue reading...

data.title: The Liberation review – Carrie Coon joins all-female cult in unsettling drama
data.description: Toronto film festival: Director Guy Nattiv draws on personal experience for an 80s-set tale of a woman abandoning her family for a creepy commune We remain fascinated and horrified by the hows and whys of cult narratives, how someone could be so seduced by something so unknown and why they would then risk everything for it. Oscar-winning writer-director Guy Nattiv has been personally affected by these questions for most of his life, his grandmother joining a cult when he was a child and never coming back. His attempt to try to understand who she was and why she acted in such a way has led to unsettling drama The Liberation, a fictionalised tale that acts as a form of therapy for him and a mostly successful antidote to more sensationalist cult stories for us. Enough Netflix docuseries and schlocky horror movies have given us a more extreme and often violent idea of how cults infect and destroy vulnerable people but Nattiv opts for a more thoughtful slow-burn. He’s recruited a suitably thoughtful actor in Carrie Coon, no stranger to this particular psychology having broken out in The Leftovers, one of the more intelligent cult dramas in recent years. The Liberation is screening at the Toronto film festival and will be released later this year Continue reading...

data.title: Resident Evil review – Zach Cregger’s rebooted action horror is a wild rollercoaster ride
data.description: The Weapons director delivers a seat-edge thriller with a standout lead performance from Austin Abrams as an everyman navigating chaos Typically horror fans react to blatant on-screen stupidity with vocal derision. Don’t go in there! Girl, get out of the house! Guys, ignore that distress signal! But genre aficionados may find themselves falling a little bit in love with Bryan (Austin Abrams), the hapless de facto hero of the new horror film Resident Evil. It’s not that Bryan is traditionally hunky, or even a caricatured version of a square-jawed warrior, like Bruce Campbell in his later Evil Dead outings. But Abrams is in possession of a Campbell-ish charm, even in the face of his character’s repeated blundering, as well as an everyman relatability that makes this wild carnival-ride movie play a little closer to the ground. Bryan is a courier – a glorified Postmates driver, in his own estimation – who postpones the end of his shift to take one last night-time run, driving an important item from one hospital to another in a snowstorm without the proper tires or four-wheel drive. After all, the distance and urgency means double pay. When he hits a mysterious woman who emerges suddenly on to a slick road, he’s drawn into a hellish outbreak that will look familiar to fans of the Resident Evil video game series (or maybe the previous six-movie Milla Jovovich franchise, which apparently drifted afield from the games’ storylines). data.title: In-I in Motion review – Juliette Binoche pulls back the curtain on dance duet with Akram Khan
data.description: The actor makes her directing debut with a raw, fascinating film about her 2008 collaboration with the British dancer In the way that wedding rehearsals can be more emotional than the big day – all the untidy feelings that will be tucked away for the cameras still on show – this documentary from Juliette Binoche feels raw and unguarded. It goes behind the scenes of Binoche’s collaboration with British dancer Akram Khan; their dance-theatre piece, a love story entitled In-I, premiered in London to mixed reviews in 2008 . Now, all these years later, Binoche makes her directing debut with a film that is essentially a study of their artistic process. And it’s unexpectedly fascinating, watching two world-famous performers pushing themselves outside their comfort zones, exposed and vulnerable – particularly Binoche, who had never danced professionally before. In-I in Motion is a film of two halves, ending with a performance on stage in front of an audience, the set designed by artist Anish Kapoor: a vast screen in murderous red. The first half is more interesting, shot fly-on-the-wall style during the months it took to create the piece in a studio. Binoche and Khan work with acting coach Susan Batson, who at one point thunders: “THIS IS FULL OF SHIT!” (never mind La Binoche’s Oscar). For some audiences, it will have a whiff of theatrical cringe; the endless stewing and fretting over how to achieve something truthful is ripe for spoof. But the pure intensity and focus is thrilling to watch. Continue reading...

data.title: Cassandra Wilson obituary
data.description: American jazz singer and songwriter who was inspired by the Delta blues and gospel sounds of her Mississippi childhood Cassandra Wilson, the double Grammy-winning jazz vocalist and songwriter who has died aged 70, was described in 2001 by Time magazine as “America’s best singer”. Superlatives accompanied Wilson throughout her career; her vocal skills supported them. Wilson’s ancestry was West African and European, and the Delta blues and gospel sounds she heard in her Mississippi childhood affected her deeply – but so did the guitar harmonies her father taught her, and the early instruction in classical piano she received from her music-teacher mother. Both her parents were Miles Davis and Motown admirers, too. Continue reading...

data.title: David Bowie: The Shel Talmy Recordings review – these unheard 60s tunes are actually pretty flimsy
data.description: (Parlophone) On this new compilation of his mid-60s Davie Jones years, Bowie can’t distinguish himself from the era’s other bands – and ends up hedging his bets In 1973, David Bowie released Pin Ups, a loving if slightly over-wrought collection of covers from the mid-60s: the moment when the previous driving forces of British pop, Merseybeat and the blues revival started giving way to something noticeably weirder, noisier and more expansive. In an accompanying promotional interview, he waxed lyrical about his memories of seeing the Pretty Things, the Who, the Creation and the nascent Pink Floyd “with dear old Syd” in impeccable mod lingo (“up the Windmill or the Elephant, get blocked, bust over to Richmond”) but tactfully neglected to mention that he was more than an amphetamine-fuelled fan: he’d wanted to be a participant, and had recorded a handful of mid-60s singles inspired by his idols. That elision shows what a strained relationship Bowie had with his pre-fame material. For most of his career, he simply tried to ignore it, although it doggedly refused to go away: his former labels kept re-releasing it, usually in sleeves that attempted to fool the buyer that it was current. Then, in his 50s, he seemed to reconsider, revisiting his 60s oeuvre on Toy, a 2001 album that was rejected by his then-label EMI – a baffling decision, if you buy the posthumous rewriting of Bowie’s history that insists his Glastonbury performance in 2000 utterly reinvigorated his career and made him as revered as he was in his peak years. Continue reading...

data.title: The Strangers by Naomi Alderman review – where has this odd new species come from?
data.description: A bereavement memoir mingles with speculative fiction, in a wise and ragged examination of grief from the author of The Power In his Remarks on Frazer’s Golden Bough, Ludwig Wittgenstein alludes to an incident that followed the death of Franz Schubert. He recalls that Schubert’s brother cut several scores into small pieces, each consisting of only a few bars of music, and handed them out to Schubert’s favourite pupils. This, Wittgenstein argues, was a totally understandable act of grief. He goes on to suggest, however, that if, in his grief, Schubert’s brother had left the scores untouched, or even burned them, then that too would be equally legible to us. Such is the disorienting nature of loss – in its wake, anything goes. In The Strangers, Women’s prize-winning author Naomi Alderman tests this thesis to its limits. How about dealing with grief by writing an uneasy memoir/speculative fiction hybrid about the sudden appearance of a new species of quasi-badgers that seem to improve the quality of local soil? data.title: The New Dark Ages by James Marriott review – a grandiose but superficial defence of reading
data.description: What is it that makes books so magical? The Times columnist somehow forgets to tell us in this lofty polemic While other kids watched cartoons, Times columnist James Marriott would spend his school holidays in bed with piles of books – “a mammoth effort of attention, perhaps the greatest I ever made” – under the spell of his father, a teacher who inculcated in him a literary zeal “not exactly common in the north of England in the early 2000s”. Twenty-five years on, Marriott fears smartphones have all but killed reading for everyone. He had to get rid of his own – “George Eliot is no match” – and now, watching the rest of us scroll, he worries not only that we will lose the ability to appreciate Middlemarch, but that we risk falling prey to tyrants and anti-vaxxers forging “a world very different to the one we have known … mystical, tribal and autocratic”. data.title: Small but mighty! Remembering the GameCube, Nintendo’s purple bundle of joy
data.description: The first console I ever bought, it was hyped as a threat to the PlayStation, then mocked as a flop. But now, as it marks its 25th anniversary, it’s looked back on with misty-eyed reverence This week marks the 25th anniversary of the Nintendo GameCube, the first console I ever bought with my own money. I vividly remember getting on the bus after school with a year’s worth of savings safely zipped into the pocket of my bag and going to a branch of Currys, where I dumped a bunch of notes, coins and vouchers on the counter to collect my pre-order. (It turned out that some of the vouchers from the previous Christmas had expired, but the guy at the checkout clearly felt so sorry for me that he redeemed them anyway. If you’re out there, Currys guy: thank you for taking pity on a desperate 13-year-old.) If it hadn’t been for the ill-fated Wii U console, whose failure to take off in 2012 resulted in the first unprofitable periods in Nintendo’s game-making history, the GameCube would be remembered as the company’s biggest flop aside from the infamous Virtual Boy, from 1995. Released in Japan this week in 2001 (and in May 2002 in Europe), this surprisingly powerful purple cube sold less than the Xbox and the PlayStation 2. With its squat, colourful form and unusual controller, arranged around a big traffic-light-green A button and small analogue sticks designed for small hands, it had a hint of Fisher-Price about it. If it hadn’t been for the ill-fated Wii U console, whose failure to take off in 2012 resulted in the first unprofitable periods in Nintendo’s game-making history, the GameCube would be remembered as the company’s biggest flop aside from the infamous Virtual Boy, from 1995. Released in Japan this week in 2001 (and in May 2002 in Europe), this surprisingly powerful purple cube sold less than the Xbox and the PlayStation 2. With its squat, colourful form and unusual controller, arranged around a big traffic-light-green A button and small analogue sticks designed for small hands, it had a hint of Fisher-Price about it. data.title: ‘Very authoritarian, very brutal’: three decades after the UK’s anti-rave crackdown, why is France doing the same?
data.description: With tear gas, grenades and a new law, French authorities are targeting unlicensed music gatherings. Those in the rave scene explore the parallels with the UK in the 90s When Spiral Tribe fled England in 1992, they left behind an indelible mark on rave history. The itinerant sound system collective are best known for their involvement with Castlemorton Common festival, an unlicensed free party drawing more than 30,000 people and lasting nearly a week. After a drawn-out and notoriously expensive trial for public order offences, Spiral Tribe were acquitted of all charges. They decided to drive their repurposed military caravans out of the UK and never look back. Their documented history often stops there. But little known is the fact that they then kicked off “the biggest illegal underground movement that Europe had ever seen”, says Spiral Tribe associate Sebastian Vaughan, AKA electronic musician 69db. data.title: Alcina review – Handel’s opera of sex and sorcery comes alive in vivid staging
data.description: Royal Opera House, London This revival of Richard Jones and Antony McDonald’s 2022 staging has kept most of its excellent original cast Lisette Oropesa is imperious and gleaming as the enchantress Alcina Handel, but make it fun. Perhaps that was Richard Jones’s brief for his production of Alcina, first seen here in 2022 and revived by Sarah Fahie, its original movement director. And of all Handel’s operas perhaps it’s this one, with its desert-island storyline of sorcery and sex – what happens on the island stays on the island – that invites this treatment. Jones makes the “good guys” into members of a kind of puritan cult, so the tension between the moral world and the sensual, instinctive one is less of a gentle pull, more a tug of war. Alcina’s prisoners are transformed by a squirt of her eponymous perfume into birds and animals – a parrot, a mandrill, a King Charles spaniel, all wearing prosthetic heads so beautifully made that for the past year or two they have been in display cases in the Royal Opera House foyer. The animals are kept busy fawning over Alcina or moving Antony McDonald’s sets around: there’s a huge bed, a greenhouse and an enchanted forest on wheeled platforms, found behind the doors of what might be a hotel corridor. It’s a wide stage, and there’s often at least one singer running across it. Amid all this, the opera’s moments of warmth, insight and introspection risk getting lost or at least overshadowed. It’s brittle, but it is entertaining. Continue reading...

data.title: Beyond Bradford and the Brontës – new walking trail shows West Yorkshire’s natural beauty
data.description: The Bradford Pennine Gateway Trail, launching this weekend, aims to ‘change  perceptions of Bradford’ by taking in the moors and the area’s new national nature reserve A grainy photograph, dated 1938, hangs in a frame on the downstairs wall of my B&B. It shows 100, perhaps 200, elegantly attired trippers sitting on the green at Shipley Glen in West Yorkshire. They’re picnicking, chatting, taking the air and enjoying the sunshine, while admiring the rocks and woods that frame the deep gully below. It’s local, low-carbon, cheap-as-chips tourism before the jet age – and also a model for how we may travel in the future. I arrived here thanks to a new trail , launching on 19 September, that runs through the also newly established Bradford Pennine Gateway national nature reserve – astonishingly, the first reserve of this kind to be created in West Yorkshire. The trail uses almost the same name and is a savvy bit of sustainable planning, connecting the three towns of Ilkley, Saltaire and Haworth but, by appealing to walkers, hopefully inspiring people to explore beyond the confines of these honeypots. Continue reading...

data.title: Mascots, merchandise and Mixue: the new wave of Asian fast food chains in Australia
data.description: Since 2023, a slew of fast food and quick service restaurants from east and south-east Asia have debuted in Australia, capturing the youth market and ‘little treat’ culture On a Thursday night along Sydney’s George Street, teenagers Sasha Luangrungvilai and Livinia Boyden are looking for a “little treat” after a big day of window shopping. Although it’s Luangrungvilai’s first time at Mixue, it’s been a long-awaited visit – Boyden has been hyping up the Chinese bubble-tea juggernaut for weeks. “I love having so many dessert options for treats,” says Luangrungvilai. “It gives me a chance to try new foods which is always great.” The first Australian outpost of Mixue opened in 2023 in Sydney and now they have more than 10 locations across the country. The brand is part of a wave of fast food and quick service restaurant chains originating from east and south-east Asia that have set up shop in Australia in recent years. Continue reading...

data.title: Colorado buys 2,100-acre ranch to help save lesser prairie-chickens from decline
data.description: Colorado’s lesser prairie-chicken population has fallen from more than 80,000 birds in 1975 to only 89 breeding males in 2024. The Southern Plains Land Trust has acquired nearly 2,100 acres for just under $2 million to restore grassland habitat. The property, near an active breeding site, will be restored with Colorado Parks and Wildlife to support the species’ recovery.

data.description: US forces intercepted a floating refuelling station in the Eastern Pacific on September 16. This vessel allegedly supported illicit drug trafficking operations for Ecuador's Los Choneros organization. This action aimed to disrupt logistical networks supporting drug trafficking in the Western Hemisphere.

data.title: Scientists removed kangaroo rats for 13 years to reveal their hidden role in desert vegetation
data.description: Researchers conducted a thirteen-year investigation by excluding kangaroo rats from designated desert areas. The absence of these rodents led to a remarkable uptick in two specific grass species due to reduced soil disruption and seed predation. This transformation in plant life further influenced the activities of other rodents and foraging birds, effectively highlighting the indispensable role kangaroo rats play in the dynamics of desert vegetation communities.

data.title: Sydney duo finishes 9 gigs in 12 hours after helicopter, plane delays, with 15 seconds left

data.title: Former Australian miner spotted Saturn ripple in 2024; two years later, co-authored 10-sided wave
data.description: An Australian amateur astronomer made a groundbreaking observation in their backyard, discovering a colossal ten-sided atmospheric wave. This unique finding corroborated the existence of a decagon around Saturn's south pole, as confirmed by years of data from the Hubble Space Telescope. The decagon, intertwined with fierce jet streams, spans numerous atmospheric levels, shedding light on the circulatory processes within the atmospheres of these gas giants.

data.title: Britain’s butterfly boom comes with a warning for next year
data.description: Britain experienced a significant butterfly boom during the record heat of summer 2026. Over 100,000 volunteers counted nearly 1.4 million butterflies and moths across the nation. Painted ladies, a migratory species, saw their numbers surge by 335 percent this season. Experts warn this boom could lead to a population crash for caterpillars next year. Drought conditions that benefited adult butterflies harmed their offspring and food sources.

Researchers once thought that dinosaurs were sluggish, cold-blooded creatures. Later findings challenged that, suggesting that older dinosaurs were warm-blooded and could control their body temperature.
Most scientists agree that Tyrannosaurus rex was warm-blooded, but pinning down the exact core temperature of an extinct creature is difficult.

Por isso, vira e mexe saio em busca de um bom almoço executivo para trazer para este espaço. Depois de ver a indicação de amigos, decidi conhecer o Limão e Brasa, casa voltada a preparos na churrasqueira a carvão. Chamou a atenção o fato de o bar estar localizado na Vila Leopoldina , bairro ainda carente de opções interessantes para comer. No dia da visita, uma quinta-feira fria e chuvosa, o lugar não estava cheio, mas bem movimentado. Leia mais (09/16/2026 - 23h00)

data.title: Escola bilíngue usa outro idioma no dia a dia e em diversas disciplinas
data.description: Aprender outro idioma na infância não significa apenas aumentar o número de aulas de uma língua estrangeira. Em uma escola bilíngue , o idioma também é usado para ensinar outras disciplinas e faz parte da comunicação do dia a dia. A diferença, porém, nem sempre é clara para as famílias, que encontram escolas bilíngues, programas bilíngues e colégios que apenas ampliam a carga horária de um determinado idioma. data.title: Inteligência artificial já é usada na maioria das escolas de ensino médio, mas país engatinha em regulação e governança
data.description: Mais da metade das escolas de ensino médio brasileiras já permite o uso de inteligência artificial generativa pelos estudantes, mas apenas 22% têm diretrizes formalizadas de boas práticas para orientar essa adoção, segundo os dados da pesquisa TIC Educação 2025, divulgada pelo Centro Regional de Estudos para o Desenvolvimento da Sociedade da Informação (Cetic.br). O reflexo dessa adoção já mobiliza discussões internas; o mesmo levantamento aponta que 8 em cada 10 escolas brasileiras debatem formalmente os impactos do uso de telas e tecnologias na saúde mental e no comportamento dos alunos. Leia mais (09/16/2026 - 23h00)

data.title: Escolas reagem à crise de saúde mental dos alunos com projetos de prevenção
data.description: O alerta vermelho para a saúde mental de estudantes acendeu entre 2021 e 2023, diante de uma avalanche, pós-pandemia, de casos como tentativas de automutilação, esgotamento extremo, crises de ansiedade aguda e até suicídios. Para frear essa onda, uma articulação entre lideranças educacionais e médicas deu origem à Comissão de Saúde Mental nas Escolas Brasileiras, que envolve 57 escolas do país. data.title: O Supremo entre as regras e o caráter
data.description: "Quando as instituições falham, o caráter prevalece." A frase é do saudoso professor e cientista político Wanderley Guilherme dos Santos e contém uma advertência fundamental. Quando regras não existem, são vagas ou deixam espaços excessivos de discricionariedade, decisões relevantes passam a depender das qualidades pessoais de quem ocupa o poder. E instituições existem, em boa medida, para que não precisemos depender disso. Leia mais (09/16/2026 - 22h00)

data.title: Aumento do apoio à democracia é boa notícia?
data.description: Parece uma boa notícia: depois de mais de uma década de retração, entre 2023 e este ano o apoio à democracia cresceu em toda a América Latina. É o que constata o relatório " Pulse of Democracy 2026 ", com os resultados da mais recente pesquisa do Lapop (Latin American Public Opinion Project), sediado nas universidades americanas de Vanderbilt e Notre Dame. O crescimento é promissor. Afinal, ocorreu em todos os grupos de idade, níveis de escolaridade e nos 14 países estudados. Leia mais (09/16/2026 - 21h08)

data.title: Henk Kroes was de man van het legendarische ‘It giet oan’ bij de laatste Elfstedentocht
data.description: Henk Kroes, de man die voorzitter was van de koninklijke Vereniging De Friesche Elf Steden toen in 1997 de laatste Elfstedentocht werd gereden, is op 87-jarige leeftijd overleden. data.title: Acute ademnood bij de bevolking en orang-oetans ernstig bedreigd: hoe verwoestende bosbranden Kalimantan teisteren
data.description: De jaarlijkse bosbranden op het Indonesische Kalimantan zijn dit keer bijzonder omvangrijk. Het vuur, gesticht voor mijnbouw en plantages en aangewakkerd door de droogte, zou al 60 procent van het leefgebied van de ernstig bedreigde orang-oetan hebben verwoest. Veel bewoners, die last hebben van de giftige rook, belanden in het ziekenhuis en krijgen zuurstof toegediend.

data.title: Heb jij geen chef-dirigent, en krijg je daar lastige vragen over? Met deze zeven stappen heb je zo weer een vaste maestro voor je neus
data.description: Goede chef-dirigenten liggen niet voor het oprapen, daar ben je al lang achter als je er eentje zoekt. Hoe vind je desondanks je ideale chef? De twee grote Nederlandse orkesten (Rotterdams en Nederlands Philharmonisch) die nu zelf zoeken geven advies: ‘Staar je niet blind op één kandidaat, maar test er meerdere tegelijk uit.’

data.title: Geen liefde, maar harde machtspolitiek: Canada past perfect bij de nieuwe strategie van Ursula von der Leyen
data.description: Europa moet in deze „openlijk vijandige” wereld vooral voor zichzelf opkomen, vindt Europese Commissievoorzitter Von der Leyen. data.title: Russophrenie in Europa: Warum wird Putin gleichzeitig überschätzt und unterschätzt?

Russland aber sei so stark, dass es schon bald die NATO angreift, heißt es parallel dazu. Wie passt das zusammen? Welche Erzählung stimmt wirklich? Oder stimmen beide nicht? data.title: Partnerstwa przemysłowe to klucz do bezpieczeństwa
data.description: Ważne jest wzmocnienie przemysłu obronnego w Polsce, ale to nie wystarczy, żeby obrona była skuteczna. Ważna jest też współpraca międzynarodowa w regionie pomiędzy mocnymi, silnymi graczami z uwzględnieniem mniejszych firm. To wszystko razem powinno stworzyć odporny, silny, rozwijający się, innowacyjny ekosystem przemysłu obronnego, przygotowanego zarówno na czas kryzysu, jak i gotowego do kontynuowania rozwoju w czasie pokoju – mówi Małgorzata Darowska, Dyrektor ds. Europejskich w Grupie WB.

data.title: Ukrajina poškodila rafinerii v Jaroslavli, ruské útoky zasáhly Kyjev a Oděsu
data.description: Počet zraněných po nočních ruských vzdušných úderech na Kyjev stoupl na 18, jsou mezi nimi i dvě děti, uvedl starosta města Vitalij Kličko. Při útocích na Oděskou oblast utrpělo zranění dalších sedm lidí, oznámily tamní úřady. Ukrajinský prezident Volodymyr Zelenskyj uvedl, že Rusko zasáhlo také energetickou infrastrukturu v Sumské a Oděské oblasti, a potvrdil, že ukrajinské síly poškodily rafinerii v ruské Jaroslavli a zasáhly leteckou základnu v Rostově na Donu.

data.title: Koalice se dohodla na snížení schodku, zrušit poplatky ČT zkusí až po volbách
data.description: Vládní koalice ANO, SPD a Motoristů sobě se dohodla na snížení návrhu schodku státního rozpočtu na příští rok v řádu jednotek miliard korun oproti původním 389 miliardám korun. data.title: Merzovi hrozí tři volební rány v řadě. Bude vrávorat a už se nezvedne, věští experti
data.description: Dvojice nedělních zemských voleb v Německu otřese pozicí kancléře Friedricha Merze. Pokud v Meklenbursku-Předním Pomořansku vyhraje Alternativa pro Německo (AfD) a v Berlíně strana Levice, bude debata o jeho budoucnosti ještě ostřejší než dosud a udržet se ve funkci bude pro Merze těžké, říká politolog Wolfgang Muno. Podle politoložky Julie Reuschenbachové ale nelze čekat, že by Merz hned v pondělí rezignoval.

data.title: Propustí soud vraha Vocáska? Psycholožka to nedoporučuje, spolek odvolal záruku
data.description: Okresní soud v Mostě ve čtvrtek rozhoduje o žádosti o podmínečné propuštění doživotně odsouzeného vraha Zdeňka Vocáska (dnes Navrátila). Jeho loňské žádosti vyhověl, což odmítla žalobkyně, která následně uspěla se stížností u krajského soudu. Spis se tak vrátil do Mostu k novému projednání. A zatímco před rokem zněla na Vocáska spíše chvála, při opětovném jednání nikoli. Soud proto nechal doplnit posudky, jejichž závěry dnes znalci soudu prezentují.

data.title: Muž zkolaboval před nádražím. Zatímco ho zachraňovali, někdo mu ukradl batoh
data.description: Terčem zloděje se v Jaroměři na Náchodsku nejspíš stal muž v bezvědomí, který zkolaboval před vlakovým nádražím. Zatímco jiní lidé poskytovali první pomoc, kdosi odcizil jeho batoh. Policisté batoh našli a podle kamerových záběrů i čtyřiačtyřicetiletého muže, který jej zřejmě odnesl. Uvnitř však chybělo 600 eur, které tam poškozený údajně měl. Podezřelému hrozí dvouletý trest.

data.title: Česká pirátská strana (Piráti)
data.description: Česká pirátská strana (Piráti) vznikla v roce 2009 po vzoru zahraničních pirátských stran. V září 2024, po sérii neúspěšných voleb, rezignovalo vedení strany včetně předsedy Ivana Bartoše. S přestávkami stranu vedl 15 let. V listopadu 2024 se do čela strany postavil náměstek pražského primátora Zdeněk Hřib.

data.title: Lesní bar vybrali zloději už poněkolikáté, policie pátrala po muži v tričku Škwor
data.description: Kolikrát se už lesní bar u Rovného na Žďársku ocitl bez zboží, peněz a často i v dezolátním stavu, už jeho provozovatelé ani nepočítají. Poprvé ho zloděj vykradl a poničil v roce 2023, další ataky pak následovaly. Muže, který v zařízení řádil tento víkend, zachytila fotopast. Hledali jej policisté, kteří ho na základě zveřejněné výzvy ztotožnili.

data.title: VIDEO: Druhá seniorka ve studni během týdne. Záchrana přišla na poslední chvíli
data.description: Jen několik dní po záchraně seniorky z desetimetrové studny v Moravských Knínicích řešili záchranáři takřka totožný případ na Hodonínsku. V Dubňanech zaslechli sousedé slabé volání o pomoc a objevili starší ženu v osm metrů hluboké studni. Záchrana trvala přibližně dvacet minut, seniorka však krátce před vytažením upadla do bezvědomí. Záchranáři ji transportovali do nemocnice v Hodoníně.

data.title: Spotřeba uhlí bude letos rekordní, na vině je drahý plyn, upozorňuje agentura
data.description: Uhlí mělo v letošním roce začít ze světové energetiky pomalu ustupovat. Vývoj na trzích ale tento předpoklad obrátil. Podle nejnovější zprávy Mezinárodní energetické agentury (IEA) má globální spotřeba uhlí v letošním roce vzrůst o 1,2 procenta a dosáhnout rekordních 8,94 miliardy tun. Jedním z hlavních důvodů jsou vysoké ceny zemního plynu, kvůli kterým některé země znovu více využívají uhelné elektrárny.

data.title: Estudo confirma menos água em rios, lagos e glaciares
data.description: Em 2025, os rios de todo o mundo enfrentaram um dos anos mais secos das últimas três décadas. O estudo da Organização Meteorológica Mundial (OMM) avisa que a quantidade de água doce armazenada à superfície ou no subsolo ficou 42 por cento abaixo da média. O ciclo da água está a tornar-se mais errático e imprevisível, por causa dos impactos da crise climática.

Brent crude futures dropped 19 cents, or 0.2 percent, to $105.64 a barrel by 06:47 a.m. Saudi time, while US West Texas Intermediate futures were down 33 cents, or 0.3 percent, at $102.10. Both contracts fell about $3 on Wednesday.

data.description: WASHINGTON, United States: The US Federal Reserve on Wednesday raised interest rates for the first time since 2023, defying President Donald Trump’s demand for cuts, as central bank chief Kevin Warsh stressed the need to combat inflation that has been “too high” for “too long.” The Fed’s Federal Open Market Committee voted unanimously to raise rates by 25 basis points to between 3.75 and 4.00 percent, saying the rate hike would support a “timelier return” to its two-percent target for inflation.

data.title: La ideación suicida en adolescentes aumentó 56% en un año
data.description: Los casos atendidos por Cecodap pasaron de 173 en el primer semestre de 2024 a 271 en el mismo período de 2025. María Elena Padrón cuenta cómo el aislamiento, el insomnio, la ansiedad y el ciberacoso precedieron la muerte de su hijo Daniel Alejandro, de 18 años de edad. Expertos advierten que el acoso escolar, la violencia, los conflictos familiares, la ansiedad y la falta de herramientas para afrontar el sufrimiento pueden aumentar la vulnerabilidad de niños y jóvenes. The post La ideación suicida en adolescentes aumentó 56% en un año appeared first on EL NACIONAL .

data.title: Personas con autismo en Venezuela enfrentan barreras económicas, educativas y de acceso a terapias
data.description: La Encuesta TEA 2026, con 2.082 respuestas de familias de todo el país, muestra un escenario de alta vulnerabilidad para niñas, niños y adolescentes en el espectro autista. Seis de cada diez hogares viven con ingresos inferiores a una canasta básica, 39,1% de los menores no tiene acceso a terapias y más de la mitad de las familias reportó experiencias de discriminación. The post Personas con autismo en Venezuela enfrentan barreras económicas, educativas y de acceso a terapias appeared first on EL NACIONAL .

data.title: LES HIRONDELLES ONT CHOISI LEURS AILES
data.description: De trente-trois espoirs, il n'en reste plus que vingt-cinq. Vingt-cinq noms, vingt-cinq destins, vingt-cinq serments faits au drapeau. Le tamis a fait son œuvre, implacable et juste. Le sélectionneur, Patrick Sangwa Mayani , l'homme à la chemise couleur de braise, a tranché. Non sans déchirement, non sans cette cruauté nécessaire qui fait les grands chefs. La présélection n'était qu'une promesse ; la liste définitive est un acte de foi.

data.title: Retail et Digitalisation: Le Guide
data.description: Digitalisation du retail : stratégies omnicanales et IA pour transformer vos magasins. Guide complet de la transformation digitale en 2026. La transformation digitale n'est plus une option pour les détaillants : c'est une nécessité. Au cours de la dernière décennie, nous avons assisté à des changements radicaux dans le secteur du retail. L'adoption généralisée de nouvelles technologies, l'évolution des comportements des consommateurs et l'accélération provoquée par la pandémie de 2020 ont contraint les enseignes à se réinventer. Aujourd'hui, nous savons que les clients utilisent en moyenne six points de contact avant d'effectuer un achat. Pour rester compétitifs, nous devons créer des expériences omnicanales fluides, intégrer les données clients et exploiter l'intelligence artificielle. Ce guide explore comment nous pouvons transformer notre approche du retail en ligne et hors ligne. Découvrez aussi les opportunités dans le secteur du parions sport en ligne pour comprendre les enjeux de la digitalisation cross-secteurs. Pourquoi La Digitalisation Est Devenue Incontournable Pour Les Détaillants Nous faisons face à une réalité simple : les détaillants qui n'investissent pas dans la digitalisation perdent du terrain face à la concurrence. Les clients d'aujourd'hui recherchent de la simplicité, de la cohérence et de la personnalisation à chaque interaction. Selon les données que nous avons compilées, les clients multicanaux dépensent quatre fois plus en magasin et dix fois plus en ligne que ceux qui utilisent un seul canal. C'est le pouvoir de l'omnicanal. La digitalisation apporte aussi une meilleure analyse des données, nous permettant de mieux comprendre et anticiper les besoins de nos clients. Elle modernise notre technologie, renforce la fidélisation et augmente les ventes. Elle réduit aussi les inefficacités opérationnelles. Cette évolution concerne également les secteurs des services numériques, où des plateformes comme le casino québec en ligne illustrent l'importance d'une expérience utilisateur optimisée, accessible sur différents appareils et basée sur des interactions personnalisées. La transformation digitale n'est pas qu'une question de vendre en ligne : c'est l'intégration fluide des canaux physiques et numériques pour créer une expérience cohérente. Les Technologies Clés Qui Révolutionnent Le Retail Moderne Pour transformer notre secteur, nous avons besoin de technologies performantes et flexibles. Les solutions modernes pour les magasins doivent être capables de s'adapter rapidement aux évolutions du marché. Parmi les outils les plus puissants, nous trouvons le commerce unifié, les applications mobiles, les systèmes de paiement intégrés et les architectures composables qui centralisent les données et les canaux. La réalité augmentée et les chatbots enrichissent aussi l'expérience d'achat. Ce qui compte vraiment, c'est d'avoir la bonne technologie en place pour accélérer la transformation et créer un lien critique entre tous les éléments de nos opérations. E-Commerce Et Omnicanal Le commerce omnicanal est devenu un standard attendu par nos clients. Nous devons assurer la continuité entre le site web, l'application mobile et le magasin physique. Le clic and collect, le ship-from-store et les dispositifs BOPIS gagnent en maturité et offrent des solutions logistiques stratégiques. Les prix, la sélection de produits et les informations doivent être cohérents sur tous les points de contact. C'est cette synchronisation qui crée une expérience d'achat fluide et nous permet de rester pertinents dans un marché en constante évolution. Intelligence Artificielle Et Personnalisation L'IA est en train de transformer la manière dont nous servons nos clients. Nous l'utilisons pour générer des recommandations personnalisées, prévoir la demande et automatiser le service client. La personnalisation évolue vers une logique prédictive et hyperpersonnalisée fondée sur des données unifiées. En magasin, nous synchronisons les stocks, les historiques clients et les prix pour offrir une expérience vraiment adaptée. Cela ne génère pas seulement une satisfaction de base : cela crée une expérience différenciée qui renforce la fidélité et la conversion. Les Défis Et Opportunités De La Transformation Numérique La transformation digitale peut être une opération coûteuse en temps et en argent. Nous devons surmonter des défis : l'intégration des systèmes, l'unification de la donnée client, la gestion des stocks et le contrôle des risques liés aux outils d'IA. La résistance au changement est aussi un enjeu majeur que nous devons gérer avec nos équipes. Cependant, les opportunités sont énormes. Nous voyons une meilleure conversion, une optimisation logistique accrue et un service client plus automatisé. Nos collaborateurs bénéficient d'outils qui leur permettent de maximiser leur impact et de prendre des décisions plus pertinentes grâce à l'analyse en temps réel. Les détaillants qui adoptent cette approche se positionnent pour réussir à long terme et offrir une croissance durable par la technologie. Conclusion La digitalisation du retail représente aujourd'hui un levier essentiel pour répondre aux nouvelles attentes des consommateurs et construire des expériences plus connectées. Les enseignes capables d'intégrer efficacement l'omnicanal, l'intelligence artificielle et l'analyse des données pourront mieux anticiper les besoins de leurs clients. Cette transformation ne consiste pas seulement à adopter de nouvelles technologies, mais à repenser l'ensemble du parcours d'achat pour créer davantage de valeur. À l'avenir, les acteurs du retail qui sauront combiner innovation, personnalisation et efficacité opérationnelle disposeront d'un avantage durable dans un marché en constante évolution. Cet article Retail et Digitalisation: Le Guide est apparu en premier sur Journalducameroun.com .

Nous l'utilisons pour générer des recommandations personnalisées, prévoir la demande et automatiser le service client. La personnalisation évolue vers une logique prédictive et hyperpersonnalisée fondée sur des données unifiées. En magasin, nous synchronisons les stocks, les historiques clients et les prix pour offrir une expérience vraiment adaptée. Cela ne génère pas seulement une satisfaction de base : cela crée une expérience différenciée qui renforce la fidélité et la conversion. Les Défis Et Opportunités De La Transformation Numérique La transformation digitale peut être une opération coûteuse en temps et en argent. Nous devons surmonter des défis : l'intégration des systèmes, l'unification de la donnée client, la gestion des stocks et le contrôle des risques liés aux outils d'IA. La résistance au changement est aussi un enjeu majeur que nous devons gérer avec nos équipes. Cependant, les opportunités sont énormes. Nous voyons une meilleure conversion, une optimisation logistique accrue et un service client plus automatisé. Nos collaborateurs bénéficient d'outils qui leur permettent de maximiser leur impact et de prendre des décisions plus pertinentes grâce à l'analyse en temps réel. Les détaillants qui adoptent cette approche se positionnent pour réussir à long terme et offrir une croissance durable par la technologie. Conclusion La digitalisation du retail représente aujourd'hui un levier essentiel pour répondre aux nouvelles attentes des consommateurs et construire des expériences plus connectées. Les enseignes capables d'intégrer efficacement l'omnicanal, l'intelligence artificielle et l'analyse des données pourront mieux anticiper les besoins de leurs clients. Cette transformation ne consiste pas seulement à adopter de nouvelles technologies, mais à repenser l'ensemble du parcours d'achat pour créer davantage de valeur. À l'avenir, les acteurs du retail qui sauront combiner innovation, personnalisation et efficacité opérationnelle disposeront d'un avantage durable dans un marché en constante évolution. data.title: Crise dans les universités : Fame Ndongo convoque à nouveau le Synes ce 17 septembre après leur premier boycott
data.description: © (Archives) C'est la 2ème tentative. Après avoir boycotté la réunion du 11 septembre, le Synes est à nouveau convoqué par le ministre d'État Jacques Fame Ndongo, ce jeudi 17 septembre à 16h00, au ministère de l’Enseignement supérieur. Cette nouvelle convocation du 16 septembre intervient alors que huit universités d'État sont en grève totale et illimitée depuis le 3 septembre 2026 sous le mot d'ordre "rentrée académique morte". Les enseignants revendiquent une dette académique de 15,4 milliards FCFA accumulée de 2000 à 2021. Selon le MINESUP, seulement 41% soit 6,35 milliards ont été payés depuis octobre 2025, il reste 9,14 milliards. Le ministère dit avoir privilégié Bamenda, Buea et Maroua. Le Synes exige le paiement intégral. Aussi, ils revendiquent l'allocation de modernisation de la recherche bloquée depuis fin 2025. Près de 80% des enseignants n'ont pas perçu la 4ème tranche. Et tous attendent les tranches de l’année 2026. Convoque pour le 11 septembre dernier aux concertations, le Synes a répondu absent. Dans sa lettre du 10 septembre, la secrétaire générale du Synes, Pr Wogaing Fotso Jeannette, avait invoqué 3 griefs : délai trop court, ordre du jour flou sans les revendications de fond, et composition de sa délégation imposée par le ministère. Le syndicat avait lui-même proposé de se revoir entre le 15 et le 18 septembre. Cette réunion du 17 septembre à 16h est donc la réponse de Fame Ndongo à cette proposition. Mais le Synes vient aussi de sanctionner 2 de ses cadres à Bamenda et Buea pour avoir participé sans mandat à la réunion du 11 septembre, preuve que la ligne dure est maintenue. Cet article Crise dans les universités : Fame Ndongo convoque à nouveau le Synes ce 17 septembre après leur premier boycott est apparu en premier sur Journalducameroun.com .

data.title: Convention du MRC 2026 : trois candidats pour succéder à Maurice Kamto
data.description: © (DR) La page Kamto se tourne. Qui pour reprendre le flambeau du Mouvement pour la renaissance du Cameroun ? Le procès-verbal de clôture des candidatures du 16 septembre révèle le trio qui s'affrontera le 17 octobre prochain à Yaoundé. Trois candidats se présentent à présidence du Mouvement pour la renaissance du Cameroun. Ronnie Bris Djolako est le premier à se jeter à l'eau. Il a déposé son dossier déposé le 16 septembre à 11h15. Sa liste est la seule avec un poste vacant de 5ème vice-président, signe d'une candidature montée rapidement. Il s'entoure de Tamesse Janvier comme n°2 et Ayissi Francois au secrétariat général, un poste stratégique. Un profil qui mise sur la continuité de l'appareil. Tiriane Balbine Nadège Noah, a déposé son dossier à 17h19. C'est l'unique femme candidate à la présidence nationale. Une candidature forte symboliquement dans un parti souvent critiqué pour son machisme politique. C’est elle qui assure l’intérim depuis la démission du président et son premier vice. Elle mise sur un ticket paritaire : quatre hommes, deux femmes dans sa vice-présidence avec Saadou Aissatou en 5ème vice-président. Son secrétaire général pressenti est Ndong Christopher Mveh. Il semble proche de l'aile "renouveau". Pierre Emmanuel Binyam est le dernier à déposer son dossier mais avec la liste la plus complète. C'est la liste la plus structurée et complète sur le papier avec huit noms sans vacance. Il place Boutche Jean Pierre Doualare en 1er vice-président et Kamche Wappi Célin au secrétariat général. Un ticket qui sent l'expérience organisationnelle. Fait notable : aucune liste ne porte le nom du Président sortant, Maurice Kamto, confirmant son retrait annoncé de la présidence du parti. Les trois listes s'affrontent pour huit postes : un président + 5 vice-présidents + secrétaire général + trésorier. Le secrétariat général rappelle que l'enregistrement ne vaut pas validation. Rendez-vous le 17 octobre à Odja. Le MRC va-t-il choisir l'expérience, la rupture ou la parité ? Listes en lice pour la convention extraordinaire du 17 octobre 2026 - Kamto ne se représente pas Liste Djolako Ronnie Bris - Président National : Djolako Ronnie Bris - 1er Vice-Président : Tamesse Janvier - 2ème Vice-Présidente : Tinack Dorothée - 3ème Vice-Président : Elias Mba - 4ème Vice-Président : Fone Serge - 5ème Vice-Président : - Secrétaire Général : Ayissi Francois - Trésorier National : Rogers Akoum[Vacant] Liste Noah Tiriane Balbine Nadège - Présidente Nationale : Noah Tiriane Balbine Nadège - 1er Vice-Président : Simh Emmanuel - 2ème Vice-Président : Ngompe Fotso Elie - 3ème Vice-Président : Kaigama Ismael - 4ème Vice-Président : Same Kolle Samuel - 5ème Vice-Présidente : Saadou Aissatou - Secrétaire Général : Ndong Christopher Mveh - Trésorier National : Oko Appolinaire Legrand Liste Binyam Pierre Emmanuel - Président National : Binyam Pierre Emmanuel - 1er Vice-Président : Boutche Jean Pierre Doualare - 2ème Vice-Président : Mbida Ndoumbe Michel - 3ème Vice-Présidente : Ndongho Sarah Laure - 4ème Vice-Président : Kouatte Elokan Paul - 5ème Vice-Président : Epie Hawkins Ejebe - Secrétaire Général : Kamche Wappi Célin - Trésorier National : Tekem Demanou Patrick. Cet article Convention du MRC 2026 : trois candidats pour succéder à Maurice Kamto est apparu en premier sur Journalducameroun.com .

data.title: MINTOUL : le Comité de l’accord tripartite sur la sécurisation des documents installé
data.description: © DR Le secrétaire général du ministère du Tourisme et des Loisirs, NDIORO A MAMOUM, a installé le 15 septembre 2026 le comité chargé de finaliser l'accord tripartite entre le Mintoul, l'Imprimerie nationale et Impact Palmarès Printing Cameroon pour la sécurisation des documents officiels. La traçabilité des documents officiels en chantier. Le comité chargé de finaliser l'accord tripartite entre le ministère du Tourisme et des Loisirs, l'Imprimerie nationale et Impact Palmarès Printing Cameroon a été installé. Créé par la décision n°00192 du 9 septembre 2026 du Mintoul, cet accord tripartite a pour objectif de garantir la sécurité, l'authenticité, la traçabilité et la bonne conservation des documents officiels au sein du ministère. Présidé par le Secrétaire Général du Mintoul, M. NDIORO A MAMOUM, au nom du ministre, ce comité a réuni les membres de l'équipe technique tripartite afin d'examiner le projet d'accord. L'objectif était de s'assurer que tous les aspects techniques, opérationnels et juridiques pertinents soient correctement pris en compte. Les discussions ont également porté sur la collecte et la validation des informations, la consolidation des contributions des différentes parties prenantes, ainsi que la préparation des éléments finaux de l'accord et de ses annexes. Ces consultations s'inscrivent dans le cadre des efforts du ministère pour renforcer les accords institutionnels et améliorer l'efficacité des services qui soutiennent le secteur du tourisme. Le processus prévoit ensuite des consultations avec les services déconcentrés du Littoral et les acteurs du secteur, avant la signature définitive. Cet article MINTOUL : le Comité de l’accord tripartite sur la sécurisation des documents installé est apparu en premier sur Journalducameroun.com .

data.title: Feicom-Guichet climat : 10,1 milliards de F pour 79 communes du Cameroun contre le changement climatique
data.description: © DR Le Fonds spécial d'équipement et d'intervention intercommunal (Feicom) passe à la vitesse supérieure face à l'urgence climatique. Plus de 10 milliards FCFA viennent d'être débloqués pour financer les projets verts des communes camerounaises. Réuni en sa 2ème session le jeudi 27 août 2026 au siège du Feicom à Yaoundé, le Comité des Concours financiers en faveur des communes dédié au Guichet climat (CCFF-C), sous la présidence du directeur général Philippe Camille AKOA, a frappé fort. Le Comité a octroyé une enveloppe globale de 10 110 000 000 FCFA (dix milliards cent dix millions) à 79 Communes réparties dans les dix (10) régions du Cameroun. Cet argent va financer des projets concrets de mesures d'atténuation et d'adaptation aux changements climatiques. Les 79 projets ont été sélectionnés à l'issue d'un appel à projets lancé le 24 juin 2026 et clôturé le 07 août 2026. Pour être éligibles, les Collectivités territoriales décentralisées (CTD) devaient répondre à l'une des quatre problématiques prioritaires identifiées par le Feicom : forêts et biodiversité ; mix énergétique ; gestion et valorisation des déchets ; infrastructures, eau et assainissement. Dans son communiqué final en date du 27 août et rendu public ce 16 septembre, le Comité s'est réjoui de "l'implication des Collectivités territoriales décentralisées (CTD) pour ce programme innovant". Les membres du CCFF-C ont toutefois relevé la nécessité de "continuer la sensibilisation pour l'identification par celles-ci, des réponses idoines aux risques et défis imposés par les changements climatiques, au profit de leurs populations". Avec ce Guichet climat, le Feicom, certifié ISO 9001/14001/45001, confirme son rôle de bras financier de la décentralisation et positionne les communes en première ligne de la lutte contre les inondations, la déforestation et la précarité énergétique qui frappent le pays. Cet article Feicom-Guichet climat : 10,1 milliards de F pour 79 communes du Cameroun contre le changement climatique est apparu en premier sur Journalducameroun.com .

data.title: Partenariat Cameroun-IsDB : l’UNICEF mise sur l’impact humain
data.description: © DR 80% des partenariats internationaux passent à côté de l'essentiel. C'est pour changer cette trajectoire que l'UNICEF Cameroon a participé activement à la Journée de la Banque Islamique de Développement le 14 septembre 2026 à Yaoundé. Le développement ne se construit pas en vase clos. Ils se concentrent sur les chiffres, les contrats et les financements, mais oublient l'impact humain réel sur le terrain. C'est précisément pour changer cette trajectoire que l'UNICEF Cameroon a participé activement à la Journée de la Banque Islamique de Développement (IsDB Group Day). Pourquoi ce rendez-vous est-il crucial ? Pour transformer durablement la vie des enfants et des communautés vulnérables, la volonté seule ne suffit pas. Il faut des alliances stratégiques solides. À travers cette journée dédiée au renforcement du partenariat entre le Cameroun et le Groupe IsDB, nous ne parlons pas seulement d'opportunités de financement. Nous parlons de priorités nationales de développement avec alignement direct sur les besoins réels, de financements à fort impact pour l'éducation, la santé et la protection de l'enfance, et de synergie d'action pour co-créer des solutions concrètes. Lorsque des acteurs majeurs comme l'IsDB et l'UNICEF unissent leurs forces aux côtés du gouvernement camerounais, les opportunités financières se traduisent directement en vies transformées : des salles de classe construites, des accès à l'eau potable garantis et un avenir restauré pour des milliers d'enfants. Cet article Partenariat Cameroun-IsDB : l’UNICEF mise sur l’impact humain est apparu en premier sur Journalducameroun.com .

data.title: 70e Conférence Générale de l’AIEA : le Cameroun affiche ses avancées nucléaires à Vienne
data.description: © DR Chef de la délégation camerounaise à la 70e session ordinaire de la Conférence Générale de l'AIEA à Vienne, la ministre Madeleine Tchuinté a présenté le 15 septembre 2026, devant 4000 représentants de 182 pays, la Déclaration du Cameroun saluant une coopération fructueuse. En sa qualité de Chef de la Délégation camerounaise aux travaux de la 70e session ordinaire de la Conférence Générale de l'AIEA qui se déroule du 14 au 18 septembre 2026 à Vienne en Autriche, Madame le Ministre de la Recherche Scientifique et de l'Innovation, Dr Madeleine Tchuinté a présenté la Déclaration du Cameroun. Devant un parterre constitué de 4000 représentants de 182 pays, elle a salué la coopération entre le Cameroun et l'AIEA en mettant un accent sur les activités menées au cours de l'année 2026. Il s'agit notamment du renforcement du cadre législatif et réglementaire en matière de sécurité et de sûreté nucléaires à travers le Décret N°2026/00201 du 02 février 2026 fixant les redevances et taxes sur les rayonnements ionisants, de l'étude de faisabilité sur le nucléaire civil, dans le double souci d'assurer sa souveraineté énergétique et de s'arrimer à l'objectif de neutralité carbone.
